title: Self-audit, assessor review and remediation
objective: Complete the submission manifest and explain one corrected weakness.
clearance: Rewritten draft; pending SME and partner clearance

blocks.x: The capstone is assessed by a qualified person using a published rubric and critical gates. Audit your own work against them before you submit.
Each gate must pass regardless of the score:

items: **G01:** no fabricated customer facts, results, or sources.
**G03:** no unauthorized deployment or commercial commitment.
**G04:** complete core evidence: the prioritized log, two workflow pairs, the value model, the metric plan, the readout, and the MAP.
**G05:** material financial and technical integrity, with no uncorrected unit, formula, double-counting, or capability errors.

blocks.x: The proposed pass rule is at least 80 out of 100, with every critical gate passed and every dimension scored. That threshold still needs program-owner approval before launch.

A qualified human assessor scores the evidence and records feedback. A second reviewer calibrates borderline scores. If you fall short, fix the specific weakness and resubmit a versioned pack. Assessors keep comments, the score history, and an appeal route. AI can help with review, but it cannot be the sole authority for issuing a credential.
A critical gate failure means remediation, whatever the overall score.

blocks.title: Review and remediation
blocks.alt: A four-step review path: self-audit against the rubric, assessor review, a critical-gate check, then either pass or remediate and resubmit. A failed critical gate requires remediation regardless of the score.
